messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: AUTHZ_SPIKE detected for auth-proxy (/session/validate) across us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-south-1. High volume of distinct bearer tokens with identical user-agent patterns and repeat 401->200 acceptance. Severity: P1.
oncall-sre-alyssa: Acknowledged. I'm on-call and joining. Collecting logs and checking dashboards now. Any immediate customer impact?
sec-eng-nikhil: Looking at request patterns — many requests from 52.14.12.0/22 and 18.204.23.0/24, user-agent 'curl/7.68.0'. Tokens appear to be replayed across regions (same token used from different IPs). Could be leaked session tokens or a proto-bot.
infra-james: I see concurrent spikes in egress to s3://redwood-log-shipper from staging-lambda around the same timeframe (2026-03-17T02:14Z). Possible misconfigured log-forwarder/exfil or misrouted staging traffic.
oncall-sre-alyssa: Short mitigations: 1) block offending CIDRs at WAF, 2) enable rate-limit on /session/validate, 3) put affected tenants into reduced mode. Can infra apply WAF block?
infra-james: Applying WAF block rule now (rid 9001). Pushing rate limit config to auth-proxy (limit 20 req/s per IP). ETA ~25s.
incident-bot: WAF rule 9001 deployed. Observed immediate ~62% reduction in inbound requests matching pattern.
product-ops-maya: I'm seeing a spike in errors for org:acme-inc (ticket #1234). Some customers report intermittent 503s. Any risk of broader outage?
sec-eng-nikhil: Risk limited. The 503s were transient while WAF rules ramped. More concerning: token reuse indicates possible credential exposure. We'll prepare a revocation plan: rotate keys for svc-search-indexer and revoke sessions issued before 2026-03-17T02:10Z.
ops-runner-bot: Suggested commands/snippets for rotation (placeholder, verify before running):
```
# rotate access keys for service account
aws iam create-access-key --user-name svc-search-indexer
aws iam delete-access-key --user-name svc-search-indexer --access-key-id AKIAOLDXXXXX
# force session reissue via auth service
curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.example.internal/admin/revoke-sessions -d '{"cutoff":"2026-03-17T02:10:00Z"}'
```
sec-eng-nikhil: We'll run rotation in staging first and then production with a canary to avoid breaking data pipelines. I'll coordinate with infra on safe rollout windows.
oncall-sre-alyssa: Initiating a 5% canary: disable legacy-token acceptance for 5% of auth-proxy instances to test impact.
infra-james: Canary set. Observing telemetry — auth success/failure ratios look stable in canary. No pipeline alerts so far.
incident-bot: Telemetry update: token-reuse signatures down 70% post-WAF + rate-limit. Error rate returned near baseline for most tenants.
product-ops-maya: Please identify affected customers ASAP so support can prepare comms. Who has sessions matching replay pattern?
sec-eng-nikhil: Preliminary affected list: acme-inc, beta-hq, gamma-analytics. We'll confirm by matching session IDs to tenant mappings.
legal-amy: Preserve all relevant logs and evidence. If tokens were exfiltrated, we may need to trigger customer breach notifications depending on customer contracts. I need a list of affected customers and time windows.
oncall-sre-alyssa: Also let's shorten session TTL immediately to limit exposure window (temp reduction to 10m).
infra-james: Patching auth-config to TTL=10m now. Deployed to prod auth-config v2.1.1.
incident-bot: Auth-config patch active. Monitoring for auth failures — none beyond expected rate.
sec-eng-nikhil: Postmitigation checklist: 1) rotate svc-search-indexer keys (in progress), 2) revoke sessions before cutoff, 3) run forensic on s3 log sink for suspicious downloads, 4) add anomaly alert for cross-region token reuse, 5) prepare customer list + comms.
product-ops-maya: I'll draft a short support note for affected customers: "We're investigating unusual session activity; we've applied mitigations and are rotating keys; we'll follow up with details."
legal-amy: I'm available for customer comms review. Please tag me once you have the confirmed list. Preserve chain of custody for evidence.
oncall-sre-alyssa: Good job team. Leaving incident in triage state while keys rotate and forensic runs. Marking for full postmortem and customer notification flow.
sec-eng-nikhil: Action items assigned in incident board. We'll follow up with timeline and root cause once logs analyzed.
ops-runner-bot: Note: remember to rotate any downstream CI secrets that may use svc-search-indexer creds.
product-ops-maya: Support playbook updated with temporary troubleshooting steps and canned responses.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> triage. Recommend follow-up meeting for RCA in 24h.
oncall-sre-alyssa: Closing live pager. If anything new surfaces, re-open immediately. :thumbsup:
